subject: ventures/cache-control-check
professional: a web-performance / CDN engineer who debugs cache behaviour against RFC 9111 and RFC 9110 daily (and who would check Vary handling, s-maxage, and Expires parsing first)

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` (75 pass, 0 fail), then recomputed outputs independently through buildReport against RFC 9111/9110 (not the author's tests). Right: (1) `Vary: *` alone -> vary-star; (2) `Expires` == `Date` with no max-age -> expires-before-date (RFC 9111 4.2.1: freshness lifetime = Expires - Date <= 0 is stale); (3) weak `W/"a"` ETag + `Accept-Ranges: bytes` -> weak-etag finding, none with `Accept-Ranges: none` (RFC 9110 13.1.5: If-Range must not carry a weak tag); (4) `public` + Set-Cookie fires, case-insensitive. Wrong: (a) `Vary: Accept-Encoding, *` -> no finding, although RFC 9110 12.5.5 ABNF `Vary = #( "*" / field-name )` allows `*` among other members and RFC 9111 4.1 treats any member `*` as always failing to match (false negative, analyze.mjs:68 tests `vary === '*'` exact string); (b) `Expires: 0` (invalid date, which RFC 9111 5.3 says to treat as already expired) -> no finding because parseHttpDate returns null; (c) `s-maxage=60` + `Expires` -> no finding although RFC 9111 5.3 also makes a cache ignore Expires when s-maxage is present; (d) `public, private="set-cookie"` is still flagged as public+cookie and `parseCacheControl('private="a, b"')` splits the quoted list into `b"`:true (quoted-string commas, RFC 9110 5.6.4). Also expires-overridden-by-max-age fires on every response having both, even when the two agree. The seven checks it does claim are right on common inputs; the misses are in edge forms, hence 2 not 3.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README feature end to end by running it: Vary: * finding works; public+Set-Cookie works; no-store+max-age works; Expires overridden by max-age works; Expires<=Date works; weak ETag+range works; static asset without headers works; CLI `node check.mjs <url> [--json] [--timeout]` exists, exit 0/1/2 per code, probe.mjs follows no redirects as stated; index.html page parses pasted JSON, has worked example, usage opt-out, three supporting pages exist. No TODOs or stubs found. Note the CLI's `--json` output omits findings by design (page re-derives them). VENTURE.yaml stage is `prototype` and all three hypotheses are untested, which matches a finished-small scope.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/cache-control-check: 75 tests, 75 pass, 0 fail. Seeded mutation 1: analyze.mjs:129 `expiresMs <= dateMs` -> `<`: test 24 'expires-before-date fires when Expires equals Date' failed (74 pass, 1 fail). Seeded mutation 2: removed the `accept-ranges !== 'none'` guard at analyze.mjs:145: test 16 failed. Both reverted with `git checkout analyze.mjs`; `git diff --stat` and `git status --short` on the venture were clean afterward. Boundary tests are real. Gaps: no test for Vary with multiple members, `Expires: 0`, s-maxage, quoted-string directives, or the live HTTP path in probe.mjs beyond stubs (probe.test.mjs exists; network-layer body handling untested).
evidence.craft: Read analyze.mjs, check.mjs, probe.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Good: analysis is a pure function shared by CLI and page, resolve-never-reject probe, usage storage wrapped in try/catch with the opt-out kept in its own key. Defects: probe.mjs drains the entire response body with no byte cap or total deadline (`res.on('data', () => {})`; `timeout` is socket-idle only), so pointing it at a large asset downloads it all, contradicting 'headers are all this check needs'; User-Agent in probe.mjs:18 cites a retired host (duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects); parseCacheControl is a naive comma split; `hasCacheControl` is redundant where `cc['max-age'] !== undefined` already implies it; `!cc['max-age']` uses truthiness on a string; main guard `import.meta.url === file://${process.argv[1]}` breaks for relative or space-containing paths; Date.parse is accepted for non-HTTP-date strings.
evidence.claims: Backed by files: MIT licence (LICENSE), no-warranty and authorisation text (README, index.html), local-only usage count (usage.mjs, usage.test.mjs), no-redirect-follow (probe.mjs), seven named checks (analyze.mjs). Not backed: the headline claim that RFC 9111 defines `Vary: *` as meaning a response is 'never reusable from cache, for any request, by any compliant cache ... no matter how similar' and 'overrides Cache-Control entirely' (README, VENTURE.yaml, analyze.mjs detail text, index.html lede, JSON-LD, FAQ, llms.txt). RFC 9111 4.1 says a stored response with `Vary: *` always fails to match a request, which stops direct reuse but the response may still be stored and revalidated (4.3), and many CDNs behave differently; 'forever'/'ever' overstates. Also llms.txt links point to duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo, a retired hosting address, rather than marisstella.app. The README does honestly hedge 'evidence, not a determination' and the public+cookie text is carefully conditional.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job 'why isn't my CDN caching this?': a developer must clone the repo (no npm package, no hosted probe), run the CLI, copy JSON, paste it into the page, or simply read the CLI text report. The CLI report alone is usable. Real job gaps: it ignores response status (a 302, 404 or 5xx has different cacheability), `Pragma`, `no-cache`/`must-revalidate`/`private` interplay, `s-maxage`, `Authorization`-dependent caching, `Age`/`Date` skew, and does not report effective freshness lifetime, so it cannot answer the 'why not cached' question for most real causes. Good as a narrow lint of seven patterns, not as a diagnosis tool.
evidence.domain: Compared against RFC 9111 (4.1 Vary, 4.2 freshness, 5.2 Cache-Control, 5.3 Expires) and RFC 9110 (12.5.5 Vary, 13.1.5 If-Range). The weak-ETag/If-Range rule and Expires-vs-Date staleness are correct practice. Departures a CDN engineer would flag first: Vary: * overclaim and the mixed-Vary false negative; no s-maxage handling; Expires: 0 and other invalid Expires values not treated as stale; no use of status code; the notice that fires on every Expires+max-age pair is noise to a practitioner who already knows max-age wins; public+Set-Cookie is the right risk to name but ignores `private="set-cookie"` field-scoped qualifiers.

defects.what: Headline claim that RFC 9111 makes `Vary: *` 'never reusable ... ever, overrides Cache-Control entirely' overstates the spec (always fails to match, but storable and revalidatable) and is repeated in README, VENTURE.yaml, page, JSON-LD, FAQ and llms.txt
Vary containing `*` among other members (e.g. `Accept-Encoding, *`) is not detected; exact-string compare
probe drains the whole response body with no size cap or overall deadline
s-maxage ignored: Expires + s-maxage not flagged, and expires-before-date is not suppressed correctly by s-maxage
Invalid Expires such as `0` is treated as no finding; RFC 9111 5.3 says treat as already expired
Cache-Control parser splits on commas inside quoted-string values
Stale hosting URLs in llms.txt and probe User-Agent
No test for multi-member Vary, Expires: 0, s-maxage or quoted directives

verdict: A small, honest-looking, well-tested linter whose seven checks give right answers on typical inputs (75 tests pass; two seeded boundary mutations were each caught and reverted cleanly). It does not meet the bar: its flagship claim about Vary: * is stated more strongly than RFC 9111 supports and repeated in every surface, mixed Vary values and s-maxage / invalid Expires slip through, and it cannot answer 'why is my CDN not caching this' for the common causes (status code, no-cache, s-maxage). Completeness is 3 (everything it says it does works) but correctness, claims and domain are 2, so it is finished at a junior-professional level.
